title: A Salt for the Veil
premise: Ada Reyes, exiled for a storm they never meant to call, has hidden among the salt-sellers of Greyharbor until the night the border wards collapse and the stars vanish, severing the covenant that keeps the sea-realm Veyl from drowning the coast. Hunted by wardens and haunted by the sister who testified against them, Ada must gather a found family of smugglers, defrocked priests, and one very stubborn lighthouse keeper to reach the drowned altar where the covenant was first sworn. There Ada learns the covenant demands a life freely given—and that their sister has already offered hers. In the end, Ada refuses both sacrifice and duty as separate choices, binding their own storm-blood into the veil at the cost of their magic, saving both realms but returning to Greyharbor ordinary, beloved, and finally home.
about_author: Wren Villalobos is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing lighthouse logs along a disappearing coastline. They write fantasy about people who survive the impossible and then have to live with it.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Selling charms in outlawed Greyharbor, Ada feels the border wards shatter and watches the stars extinguish one by one while the tide rises unnaturally high. When wardens begin door-to-door sweeps for 'resonants,' Ada's landlady—a retired smuggler named Brannoc—shelters them and reveals she always knew what they were. Emotional beat: terror giving way to the first fragile trust in twelve years.

chapters.title: What the Tide Remembers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Ada and lighthouse keeper Sefa Ilo, who can still see the drowned realm through her lamp's glass. The group—Ada, Brannoc, Sefa, and a defrocked priest carrying the covenant's last true rite—sails toward the drowned altar pursued by wardens and things wearing drowned sailors' faces. Ada learns their exile was engineered by someone who wanted the covenant broken. Emotional beat: found family solidifying under pursuit.

chapters.title: A Salt for the Veil
chapters.summary: Ada's POV at the drowned altar. The priest reveals the covenant requires a willing death; then Ada's estranged sister Marisol arrives—she has secretly served the Veyl court for years and offers herself to restore the veil. The warden commander, revealed as the covenant's original breaker, attacks mid-rite. Climax: Ada seizes the storm they were exiled for and pours their own magic into the veil instead of a life, unmaking their power forever. Emotional beat: love refusing to be a currency.

chapters.title: Ordinary Weather
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV, weeks later. The stars return; the sea is just a sea. Magicless Ada struggles with an identity built around power they no longer have, while Marisol, spared and changed, tentatively rebuilds their bond over salt-bread and arguments. Brannoc reopens the smuggling routes; Sefa and Ada admit what the dark voyage meant. Final beat: rain falls on Greyharbor—just rain—and Ada stands in it, home, choosing the small life they once fled.
